catalog_quote: Kyirong Tibetan is an example of this second type. It has six phonemic tones and resembles Sinitic type systems by virtue of polytonicity. However, this system is complex in that vowel F0 is only one of a number of relevant correlates, summarized in Table 1. [Table 1. Kyirong Tibetan tones (Huber 2000: 22-24): High Level / High Falling / Mid Level / Mid Falling / Low Level / Low Falling] ... There are additional correlates of vowel phonation found across the three registers: Vowel phonation (modal, breathy and occasionally creaky for contour tones), and onset (obstruent) phonation for consonants. ... Other Bodish languages, like Kyirong Tibetan, are hybrid between word-tone and syllabic, with some morphemes as tonal, and others a-tonal (Huber 2002; Hall and Hildebrandt 2006). ... 6. sources.citation: Zeisler, Bettina. 2010. Review: The Tibetan dialect of Lende (Kyirong), by Brigitte Huber (Bonn: VGH 2005, xiii+345 pp). Himalayan Linguistics 9(1): 123-131. DOI 10.5070/H99124430.
sources.quote: 'One of the most remarkable phonological traits of Lende is its system of tones. Unlike most Central Tibetan varieties ... the Lende dialect does not show a binary tone distinction (high vs. low), but a ternary distinction (high, medium, low).' Reviewer praises Huber's 'well-informed treatment of phonology'; no stress or accent mentioned anywhere in the review (grep).

sources.citation: Huber, Brigitte. 2000. Preliminary report on evidential categories in Lende Tibetan (Kyirong). Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 23.2: 155-174.
sources.quote: 'In my phonological transcription [high mark] stands for high register tone and [low mark] for low register tone. In the course of future research, another feature, breathy voice, will probably turn out to be phonologically relevant.' Primary-author statement: register tone marked lexically; no stress marked or mentioned.
sources.note: Primary-author transcription note (p. 157 fn. 10): register tone marked, breathy voice likely phonemic, no stress. fetched sources now (SEAlang scan, scanned).

sources.citation: Bickel, Balthasar, Kristine A. Hildebrandt & Rene Schiering. AUTOTYP Word Domains module (autotyp-data, data/csv/Word/), LID 720 'Tibetan (Kyirong)', glottocode kyer1238.
sources.quote: All 18 Kyirong phonological-word domains (compiled by Hildebrandt from Huber's grammar and Hall & Hildebrandt 2008; DataSourceType 'Grammar Explicit/Implicit') are tone or segmental domains (contour-tone neutralization, tone defaults to H, deaspiration, voicing assimilation, cluster licensing...); CohesionPatternStressPresence = 'other' for every row, whereas the same database codes 'stress-related' domains for Lhasa Tibetan, Kham, Manange and Limbu. Indirect but pointed evidence that the primary descriptions state no word-stress domain.

Bibliographic only: confirms Hall & Hildebrandt 2008, Linguistics 46.2: 215-248, DOI 10.1515/LING.2008.010; no author PDF linked. 'Syllable and phonological word in two Tibetan dialects' (Glottolog ref 678182) does not appear in the CV publication list.
